html:
A war fought from 1715 to 1717 between the English colony of South Carolina and the Yamasee, joined by many other Native peoples of the Southeast. It nearly destroyed the colony.

Its roots were the Carolina trade in deerskins and in Native slaves. Traders cheated, beat and enslaved the people they traded with, and Native debts grew huge. In April 1715 the Yamasee killed traders and officials at Pocotaligo. Within weeks the Muscogee (Creek), Catawba and many smaller Piedmont peoples such as the Waxhaw, Congaree and Cheraw had attacked. Settlers fled to Charles Town, where food ran short.

The turn came in early 1716, when the Cherokee sided with the colony. The Yamasee moved south to Spanish Florida, and the Creek made peace in 1717.

The war changed the region. Carolina's trade in Native slaves shrank sharply. Several small peoples were broken and joined the Catawba. The settlers blamed the colony's owners for their weakness, and South Carolina was soon taken over by the Crown. Some of the peoples John Lawson had described in 1701 were gone a few years later.
sum: A war fought from 1715 to 1717 between the English colony of South Carolina and the Yamasee, joined by many other Native peoples of the Southeast. It nearly destroyed the colony.
